question: ACCELERATOR_THE_INSTANT_IS_THE_COST confirmed PER-ITERATION COALESCING as a mechanism -- rotating each lane's inner sequence costs 1.11-1.22x at 17 runs and 1.41x at 32 runs at an identical address set -- and named its own remainder: 'the CAUSE is open; the axis that would separate a coalescer width from a transaction count is the GRANULARITY of the shattering.'
THE_LADDER_COMPUTED_BEFORE_ANY_TIMING: Rotate by BLOCKS of k adjacent lanes, offset = (lane / k) mod n. Lanes inside a block share an offset so their groups stay CONSECUTIVE, and at cols=16384 with four groups per lane iteration 0's request is 32/k contiguous runs per simdgroup: 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 at k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. The per-lane group set is INVARIANT at every rung, verified over all 64 lanes for all seven, so span, fragmentation, stride and the loop-wide set are pinned exactly as before and ONLY the run count moves. rotblk64 is the CONTROL: lane/64 is 0 for every lane, so it computes the SHIPPED ORDER while paying the identical division and modulo.

P2_IS_THE_DISCRIMINATOR_AND_IT_IS_REFUTE.the_arm: k=32 is a NON-IDENTITY ORDER WHOSE EVERY SIMDGROUP ITERATION IS ONE CONTIGUOUS RUN, and it is a MINIMAL departure: simdgroup 0 is BIT-FOR-BIT the shipped order and only simdgroup 1 starts a quarter later. If the cost is what a simdgroup asks for at an instant, re-ordering WHICH contiguous request comes first is free.
P2_IS_THE_DISCRIMINATOR_AND_IT_IS_REFUTE.measured: 1.2434x and 1.2341x, losing 14 OF 14 ROUNDS IN BOTH RUNS
P2_IS_THE_DISCRIMINATOR_AND_IT_IS_REFUTE.verdict: REFUTED, five times past my own falsifier. A PERFECTLY COALESCED SIMDGROUP REQUEST STILL COSTS 24% IF THE THREADGROUP'S IS NOT CONTIGUOUS -- and that is the correction, because counting at the right width separates them: at k=32 each simdgroup issues ONE run while the THREADGROUP issues TWO, its two halves sitting in different quarters of the row. The unit that matters here is the THREADGROUP, not the simdgroup.

P1_IS_ALSO_REFUTED_AND_REPRODUCIBLY_SO.predicted: time falls MONOTONICALLY as k rises; falsifier non-monotone beyond noise, or flat
P1_IS_ALSO_REFUTED_AND_REPRODUCIBLY_SO.verdict: REFUTED. THE LADDER IS NOT MONOTONE AND THE NON-MONOTONICITY REPRODUCES: k=4 is the WORST rung in BOTH runs, worse than k=1 in run 2 and worse than every coarser rung in both, at 28.7% round-spread in the cleaner run so it is not a contamination artifact. The run count is therefore NOT the variable, which is a direct correction to reading the previous block's two points (17 runs at 1.11-1.22x, 32 runs at 1.41x) as a gradient -- two points admit a line and six points refuse one.

WHAT_THE_SIX_RUNGS_SAY_TOGETHER: THE PENALTY IS NEARLY BINARY. One contiguous THREADGROUP request costs 1.00 by construction; every departure from it costs 1.23-1.31x, and MAXIMUM shattering adds only a further ~0.2 to reach 1.44-1.49x. The single largest jump in the whole ladder is the FIRST ONE -- control to k=32, ONE threadgroup run to TWO -- at 24%, against at most another 20 points spread over the remaining thirty-one-fold increase in shattering. NEITHER CANDIDATE MECHANISM THE PREVIOUS BLOCK NAMED SURVIVES IN ITS OWN SHAPE: a TRANSACTION COUNT would be linear in runs and a COALESCER WIDTH would saturate smoothly, and a step at the first departure is neither. No third mechanism is offered -- this program's scorecard is five diagnoses written down and two wrong, and the shape was deliberately left unpredicted so it could be reported as measured.

P4_CONFIRMED_AT_THE_EDGE.predicted: k=1 reproduces the previous block's 32-run point at 1.35-1.45x
P4_CONFIRMED_AT_THE_EDGE.measured: 1.4437 (inside) and 1.4594 (0.7% ABOVE the band), against that block's 1.4095
P4_CONFIRMED_AT_THE_EDGE.verdict: CONFIRMED on one run and MISSED HIGH BY 0.7% on the other, reported rather than the band widened.

P5_CONFIRMED_AND_THE_CONTROL_IS_DIFFEREN: Every arm is a REORDERING so every arm MUST be CORRECT -- rel_err 2.512e-07 to 2.563e-07, and the control's 2.512e-07 is the LOWEST, which is what a kernel summing in the shipped association order should read. The replacements for the unavailable wrong-by-construction control: per-lane sets asserted EQUAL lane by lane AT EVERY RUNG, the order asserted DIFFERENT for k<64 and asserted NOT DIFFERENT at k=64 so the control cannot silently become an arm, a NON-POWER-OF-TWO block REFUSED because lanes must divide evenly or the run count is not 32/k, and an executing test running the generated Metal against a float64 oracle.
what_this_corrects_in_my_own_previous_tw: ACCELERATOR_THE_INSTANT_IS_THE_COST's MEASUREMENTS STAND -- rotation costs, harder shattering costs more between its two points, and the address set was identical. WHAT IS CORRECTED IS THE READING: 'per-iteration coalescing' was stated at SIMDGROUP granularity, and k=32 has perfect simdgroup coalescing and still costs 24%, so the simdgroup is the WRONG WIDTH -- which also corrects ACCELERATOR_THE_SIMDGROUP_SPAN_DOUBLES, whose central correction was to move the unit FROM the threadgroup TO the simdgroup. That move was right about the LOOP-WIDE span arithmetic and wrong as a general rule about which width the memory system charges for, and the two blocks together show the unit is not one thing to be settled once. And the cost is a STEP, not a quantity proportional to how badly the request is shattered.

controls.anti_vacuity: per-lane sets equal LANE BY LANE at every rung; order asserted different for k<64 and NOT different at k=64
controls.arithmetic: rotblk64 pays the identical division and modulo in the shipped order, so every comparison is ORDER alone
controls.correctness: every arm CORRECT at 2.51-2.56e-07 against a shared float64 oracle, with an executing test tying the formula to the generated Metal
controls.order: arm order ROTATES by round index
controls.refusal: a non-power-of-two block is REFUSED by name
controls.mutations: three watched failing -- the block divisor removed, the power-of-two check disabled, the drift guard dropped

claim_boundary: THE MECHANISM IS STILL NOT NAMED and is now harder to name, not easier: a step at the first departure fits neither of the two candidates the previous block listed, and no third is offered.

k=4 IS REPRODUCIBLY THE WORST RUNG AND IS UNEXPLAINED. A ladder with a reproducible bump in it is reported with the bump rather than smoothed, and nothing here says why 128-byte blocks should cost more than 32-byte ones.

ONE SHAPE (cols=16384, four groups per lane), ONE tpr, ONE machine, INSTANCE. The production shape CANNOT run this ladder at all -- at GROUPS=80 a lane holds two groups so only two orderings exist and k>=16 all collapse to the control, which is why the sweep is at a shape the resident does not use, stated rather than buried.

BENCH_STATE CONTENDED, round-spreads 9.7% to 317%, minima the estimator with medians beside them; the ORDINAL count is what carries the verdict and it is 84 OF 84 rounds across both runs, the strongest ordinal evidence in this family. The operator's job was NOT killed per S032 s24.

NO SHIPPED KERNEL CHANGED. Every arm is CORRECT so a reordered kernel is a legitimate candidate in principle, and every rung LOSES to the control at both runs, so nothing is adopted and the shipped order remains the best point measured on this axis.
No model executed, no capability run, no adequacy claim moves; and PRODUCTION DOES NOT PAY THE SUBMISSION TERM, unchanged.
next: The step sits between ONE threadgroup request and TWO, so the axis that would price it is the THREADGROUP WIDTH itself: at tg=64 a threadgroup IS one simdgroup and the k=32 arm would have nothing to split, while at tg=256 there are four. Sweeping tg with the same block rotation says whether the penalty is per extra request or per simdgroup that disagrees with its neighbours. NOT RUN HERE.

AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNIT_IS_THE_ROW_N.what_is_corrected: This receipt concluded 'THE UNIT THAT MATTERS HERE IS THE THREADGROUP, NOT THE SIMDGROUP'. THE FIRST HALF IS REFUTED BY THE VERY AXIS THIS RECEIPT NAMED AGAINST ITSELF. Sweeping the threadgroup width 64/128/256/512 takes the CONTROL from ONE contiguous threadgroup request to EIGHT and costs NOTHING -- 1.0000/0.9861/0.9936/1.0146 and 1.0000/1.0035/1.0068/1.0029 across two runs, at 4,5,4 and 5,10,9 of 14 ordinal rounds -- while the k=32 penalty stays 1.209x-1.267x at EVERY width, tracking the ROW's request count, which the rotation never lets tg move.
AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNIT_IS_THE_ROW_N.why_the_column_read_that_way: the 'thrd runs' column in this receipt's ladder was the ROW's count, 64/k, under the wrong label. At this receipt's own tg=128 a threadgroup holds TWO rows at unrelated base addresses, so the control's real threadgroup request was TWO runs and not the ONE recorded.
AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNIT_IS_THE_ROW_N.and_this_receipt_also_mis-stated_the_sim: its 'next' says 'at tg=64 a threadgroup IS one simdgroup ... while at tg=256 there are four'. A simdgroup on this chip is 32 lanes: tg=64 is TWO and tg=256 is EIGHT.
AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNIT_IS_THE_ROW_N.what_is_unchanged: EVERY MEASUREMENT HERE STANDS -- k=32 at 1.2434x and 1.2341x, the non-monotone ladder, k=4 reproducibly worst, 84 of 84 rounds lost -- and so does the negative half of the conclusion, that the SIMDGROUP is not the unit. What changes is where the positive half points: across three blocks the unit is excluded at 32 lanes and at 128-512 threads and located at 64 lanes, where the row, the threads-per-row and a 2-simdgroup pair COINCIDE AND ARE NOT SEPARATED.
